alternatives.argument:
Complete locally authored Definition, including all finite graph, loop, parallel-edge, endpoint-incidence, trace, and anchor conventions:

Assume the Axiom of Choice as required by the cited one-dimensional
representative interface. A **finite metric graph**
$\Gamma=(V,E,\partial_-,\partial_+,\ell)$ consists of finite vertex and
edge sets $V,E$, endpoint maps $\partial_-,\partial_+:E\to V$, and edge
lengths $0<\ell_e<\infty$. Distinct edges with the same endpoints are
allowed, as are loop edges with $\partial_-e=\partial_+e$. Every vertex is
an endpoint of at least one edge. The two endpoint incidences $(e,-)$ and
$(e,+)$ remain distinct even for a loop. A graph path is a finite sequence
$z_0,e_1,z_1,\ldots,e_n,z_n$ with $n\ge0$ and
$\{\partial_-e_j,\partial_+e_j\}=
\{z_{j-1},z_j\}$ for every $j$; a loop permits $z_{j-1}=z_j$. Vertices in
the same connected edge component are those joined by such a path. Orient
each edge only to choose its coordinate $x_e\in[0,\ell_e]$, with $0$ at
$\partial_-e$ and $\ell_e$ at $\partial_+e$. For $z\in V$, let
$\mathcal I(z):=\{(e,-):\partial_-e=z\}\cup\{(e,+):\partial_+e=z\}$
be its finite set of endpoint incidences.
The edge-product spaces are

$$H:=\bigoplus_{e\in E}L^2(0,\ell_e;\mathbb R),\qquad \mathcal W:=\bigoplus_{e\in E}H^1(0,\ell_e;\mathbb R).$$

For $w_e\in H^1(0,\ell_e)$, its endpoint values mean the values of the unique
absolutely continuous representative supplied by
[[cor-one-dimensional-w-one-p-functions-have-absolutely-continuous-representatives]].
The **trace-matching graph Sobolev space** is the subspace of $\mathcal W$
whose endpoint-incidence traces all agree at each vertex. For a designated
anchor set $D\subseteq V$, define the **anchored graph energy space**

$$V_D:=\{w\in\mathcal W:\ w_{\iota}=w_{\iota'}\text{ whenever }\iota,\iota'\in\mathcal I(v),\quad w_{\iota}=0\text{ for each }v\in D,\ \iota\in\mathcal I(v)\}.$$

We equip $H$ with the edge-sum $L^2$ inner product and $V_D$ with

$$\|w\|_{V_D}^2=\sum_{e\in E}\int_0^{\ell_e}(|w_e|^2+|w'_e|^2)\,dx_e.$$

No Kirchhoff derivative condition is built into $V_D$; that condition is a
natural boundary condition of the later weak diffusion form. The elliptic
and P1 error results below assume that $D$ meets every connected edge
component.

Complete locally authored Statement and phase-step Proof, including the endpoint-incidence extension:

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Orient each edge coordinate from $0$ at
$\partial_-e$ to $\ell_e$ at $\partial_+e$. For endpoint incidences
$(e,-)$ and $(e,+)$ define the outward derivatives by
$\partial_{\nu_{(e,-)}}u_e=-u'_e(0)$ and
$\partial_{\nu_{(e,+)}}u_e=+u'_e(\ell_e)$. The two incidences are both
included at a loop vertex. For $\iota=(e,\pm)$ write $e(\iota)=e$.
If $u_e\in H^2(0,\ell_e)$, with $H^2$ as defined by
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]],
$v\in V_D$, and each edge has a constant diffusivity $\kappa_e>0$, then

$$\sum_{e\in E}\kappa_e\int_0^{\ell_e}u'_ev'_e\,dx_e =-\sum_{e\in E}\kappa_e\int_0^{\ell_e}u''_ev_e\,dx_e +\sum_{z\in V}v(z)\sum_{\iota\in\mathcal I(z)}\kappa_{e(\iota)}\partial_{\nu_\iota}u_{e(\iota)}(z).$$

Thus zero test traces remove anchored endpoint terms, and a Kirchhoff
condition
$\sum_{\iota\in\mathcal I(z)}\kappa_{e(\iota)}\partial_{\nu_\iota}u_{e(\iota)}(z)=0$ at each free vertex
cancels the remaining terms.



**Given:** The oriented intervals, outward derivative convention, edge
diffusivities, and edge functions specified in the Statement.

1.1 If $E=\varnothing$, both sides are empty sums and the identity is $0=0$.
Otherwise fix an edge $e$. By [F1] and [F4], $u'_e$ and $v_e$ have absolutely continuous
representatives on $[0,\ell_e]$. They are bounded there. The product
$u'_ev_e$ is absolutely continuous: for any disjoint intervals $[a_j,b_j]$,
$$\sum_j|u'_e(b_j)v_e(b_j)-u'_e(a_j)v_e(a_j)| \le \|u'_e\|_\infty\sum_j|v_e(b_j)-v_e(a_j)| +\|v_e\|_\infty\sum_j|u'_e(b_j)-u'_e(a_j)|,$$
so the defining absolute-continuity condition follows from that of the two
factors. At almost every point both derivatives exist, and [F3] gives
$(u'_ev_e)'=u''_ev_e+u'_ev'_e$. These two terms are integrable by
Cauchy–Schwarz. Applying [F2] to the product therefore yields
$$\int_0^{\ell_e}u'_ev'_e\,dx_e =-\int_0^{\ell_e}u''_ev_e\,dx_e +u'_e(\ell_e)v_e(\ell_e)-u'_e(0)v_e(0).$$
The endpoint terms are the head and tail outward derivatives paired with
their traces. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

1.2 Multiply the identity of step 1.1 by $\kappa_e$ and sum over the finite
edge set. At each vertex, all endpoint-incidence values of $v$ equal the
common trace $v(z)$ by definition of $V_D$; this includes both incidences
of a loop. Regrouping the finite endpoint sum by vertices gives the displayed
identity. If $z\in D$, then
$v(z)=0$; if $z\notin D$, the stated Kirchhoff sum is zero. Hence the
boundary contribution vanishes under those conditions. [step 1.1, given, algebra] ∎

Complete locally authored Statement and phase-step Proof, including the endpoint-incidence extension:

Assume the Axiom of Choice and assume every connected edge component of the finite metric graph $\Gamma$
has at least one anchor in $D$. Put
$L_\Gamma=\sum_{e\in E}\ell_e$. Then every $w\in V_D$ satisfies

$$\|w\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}\le L_\Gamma \left(\sum_{e\in E}\|w'_e\|_{L^2(e)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$



**Given:** The finite anchored graph and the edgewise absolutely continuous
representatives of $w$.

1.1 If $E=\varnothing$, then $H=\{0\}$ and the inequality is $0\le0$.
Otherwise fix an edge $e$ in a component containing an anchor. If $e$ is a
loop, deleting its interior leaves the component connected because any path
that traverses the loop can omit that closed excursion. If its endpoints are
distinct, every original path that uses $e$ reaches one endpoint before
traversing it; after deleting $e$, vertices are therefore connected to one
of its two endpoints. Thus removing $e$ either leaves the component connected
or separates it into two components, one containing each endpoint. In the
connected case choose either endpoint; in the separated case choose the
endpoint in the component containing an anchor. By [F3] there is a finite
path from an anchor to that endpoint avoiding $e$. Deleting the portions
between repeated vertices gives a simple path, so no edge is traversed twice.
For a loop choose its tail incidence; otherwise use the incidence at the
chosen endpoint. For any $x$ on $e$, append the segment from that incidence
to $x$. The total length is at most $L_\Gamma$, and the common vertex traces
agree along the path by [F1].
Since $w=0$ at the anchor, [F1] and [F2] imply
$$|w_e(x)|^2\le L_\Gamma \sum_{a\text{ on the concatenated path}}\int_a|w'_a|^2 \le L_\Gamma\sum_{a\in E}\|w'_a\|_{L^2(a)}^2.$$
[A1, F1, F2, F3, given, choose]

1.2 Integrate the pointwise bound of step 1.1 over every edge and sum. The
total measure of the disjoint edge interiors is
$\sum_e\ell_e=L_\Gamma$, so
$$\|w\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}^2\le L_\Gamma^2\sum_{e\in E}\|w'_e\|_{L^2(e)}^2.$$
Taking nonnegative square roots proves the statement. [step 1.1, algebra] ∎
